result.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
result.comment: A thesis that discusses the coexistence of memorization and generalization in generative models
result.summary: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows, these basins shrink, and spurious states emerge as attractors that blend stored samples yet match none of them. They are the first signs of generative capability. We characterize this transition by measuring the volume, energy, and curvature of these basins across datasets and architectures, including Stable Diffusion. We then turn to language and move beyond the energy-based view of AM. We show that uniform-state discrete diffusion models are AMs capable of retrieving unseen data, with basins of attraction that arise from conditional likelihood maximization alone. As the training set grows, basins around training examples contract while basins around unseen examples expand, until corrupted test sentences are recovered as reliably as training ones. Conditional entropy exposes this coexistence within a single sequence and cheaply diagnoses where a model lies along the transition. Together, these results suggest that AM is a general principle defined by basins of attraction, and that memorization and generalization can coexist within one model. AM thus offers a framework for asking when a generative model recalls and when it creates.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文（学位论文）以能量模型与联想记忆为框架，论证扩散模型（含 uniform-state 离散扩散语言模型）可视为联想记忆：训练样本周围形成吸引盆，数据增多时盆地收缩并出现混合样本的「伪态」，作者跨数据集与架构（含 Stable Diffusion）测量盆地的体积、能量与曲率，并用条件熵诊断记忆与泛化的共存。
AI.relevance_reason: 其吸引子动力学与盆地几何描述状态如何被检索和稳定，可能为 latent 推理状态的更新与「记忆还是新生成」判别提供分析工具，条件熵式诊断也可供核查是否能用于停止决策；但该文无视觉语言推理实验，迁移性需人工判断。
